का.आ. 4662(अ).--केन्द्रीय सरकार ने, राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग अधिनियम, 1956 (1956 का 48) (जिसे इसमें इसके 
पश्चात्‌ उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 3क की उपधारा (1) के अधीन जारी की गई भारत सरकार के सड़क 
परिवहन और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 733 तारीख 16/02/2024, जो भारत के राजपत्र, 
असाधारण, भाग 11, खण्ड 3, उपखंड (1) में प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा असम राज्य के कामरूप जिले में NH27 के 
कि.मी. 0 से कि.मी.15.945 (डी.सी कार्यालय, कामरूप, अमीनगांव) तक के राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग के निर्माण (चौड़ा करने/चार 
लेन का बनाने, आदि), अनुरक्षण, प्रबंधन और प्रचालन के लिए उस अधिसूचना से उपाबद्ध अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का 
अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी ; 


और उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्तअधिनियम की धारा 3क की उपधारा (3) के अधीन तारीख २३ जनवरी 
२०२४ "को आमार असम" में अखोमिया भाषा में और द असम ट्रिब्यून " में अंग्रेजी भाषा में प्रकाशित किया गया था 


जबकि सक्षम प्राधिकारी को धारा 3-ग के तहत दायर आपत्ति प्राप्त हुई है, जिस पर विचार किया गया है और 
उसका उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (1) के अनुसरण में, केन्द्रीय सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है;

New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


9.0. 4662(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 733 Dated:16/02/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and operation 
of NH27 in the stretch of land from Km. 0 to Km. 15.945 (D.C Office, Kamrup,Amingaon) in the district of KAMRUP 
in the state of ASSAM 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Amar Asom” in Assamese 
Language and “The Assam Tribune” in English Language both dated 23 January 2024; under sub-section (3) of 
section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


70 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


9.0. 4663(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, S.O. 615 Dated:12/02/2024, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and operation 
of Rudrapur Bypass the stretch of land from Km 0.000 to Km 21.476 in the district of Rampur in the state of Uttar 
Pradesh. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Aaj” and “The Times of 
India” both dated 17.02.2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas objections have been received and the same have been considered and disallowed by the 
competent Authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government 
hereby declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule 
shall vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

का.आ. 4671(अ).-- केन्द्रीय सरकार ने पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन (भूमि में उपयोग के अधिकार का 
अर्जन) अधिनियम, 1962 (1962 का 50) (जिसे इसमें इसके पश्चात उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 3 की उपधारा 
(1) के अधीन जारी की गई भारत सरकार के पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का. आ. 
3139(अ) तारीख 02 अगस्त 2024, जो भारत के असाधारण राजपत्र तारीख 06 अगस्त, 2024, में प्रकाशित की गई थी, 
द्वारा उस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में पश्चिम बंगाल राज्य में एल पी जी परिवाहन के लिए 
हिन्दुस्तान पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड द्वारा हाल्दिया से पानागढ़ पाइपलाइन बिछाने के प्रयोजन के लिए उपयोग के 
अधिकार का अर्जन के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी; 


और उक्त असाधारण राजपत्र अधिसूचना की प्रतियां जनता को तारीख 5 सितम्बर, 2024 को उपलब्ध करा दी 
गई थी ; 

और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उपधारा (1) के अधीन केन्द्रीय सरकार को रिपोर्ट दे दी 
है; 

और केन्द्रीय सरकार ने, उक्त रिपोर्ट पर विचार करने के पश्चात, और यह समाधान हो जाने पर कि उक्त भूमि 
पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए अपेक्षित है, उसमें उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने का विनिश्चय किया है ; 


6956 GI/2024 (1) 


2 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


अतः अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उपधारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, 
यह घोषणा करती है कि इस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए उपयोग के 
अधिकार का अर्जन किया जाए ; 

और केन्द्रीय सरकार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उपधारा (4) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह 
निर्देश देती है कि उक्त भूमि में उपयोग का अधिकार इस घोषणा के प्रकाशन की तारीख से केन्द्रीय सरकार में निहित होने के 
बजाए, सभी विल्लंगमों से मुक्त होकर हिन्दुस्तान पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड में निहित होगा। 

पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन अधिनियम, 1962 की धारा 10 के अधीन किसी भी क्षतिपूर्ति के लिए 
हिन्दुस्तान पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड पूर्णतया उत्तरदायी होगी और पाइपलाइन से सम्बन्धित किसी भी मामले पर 
केन्द्रीय सरकार के विरूद्ध कोई वाद, दावा या कानूनी कार्यवाही नहीं हो सकेगी ;

New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


9.0. 4671(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Petroleum and 
Natural Gas number §.0.3139(E) dated the 2™ August, 2024, issued under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the 
Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 (50 of 1962), (hereinafter referred 
to as the said Act), published in the Extra Ordinary Gazette of India dated the 6" August, 2024, the Central 
Government declared its intention to acquire the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule appended to that 
notification for the purpose of laying pipeline for transportation of LPG from Haldia to Panagarh Pipeline in the State 
of West Bengal by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited; 


And whereas copies of the said Extra Ordinary Gazette notification were made available to the public on the 5" 
September, 2024; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has under sub-section (1) of section 6 of the said Act submitted his report 
to the Central Government; 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 5 


And whereas the Central Government, after considering the said report and on being satisfied that the said land is 
required for laying this pipeline, has decided to acquire right of user therein; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 6 of the said Act, the Central 
Government hereby declares that the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule appended to this notification is 
hereby acquired for laying the pipeline; 


And further, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 6 of the said Act, the Central 
Government hereby directs that the right of user in the said land for laying the pipeline shall, instead of vesting in the 
Central Government, vest on the date of publication of this declaration, in Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited, 
free from all encumbrances. 


Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited shall be exclusively liable for any compensation in terms of Section 
10 of the P&MP Act, 1962 and no suit, claim or legal proceeding would lie against the Central Government on any 
matter relating to the pipeline;

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


S.O. 4679(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways, 8.0. 2391 (E) Dated:20/06/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, 
Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National 
Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government 
declared its intension to acquire the land specified in the Schedule annexed to the said notification for 
building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and operation of Greenfield Expressway 
in the stretch of land from Km. 67.129 to Km. 98.989 (Gajwel) in the district of SIDDIPET in the state of 
TELANGANA 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “MANA TELANGANA” 
and “THE HANS INDIA” both dated 24/07/2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered 
and settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority 
has submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the 
powers conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that the land specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government 
hereby declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said 
Schedule shall vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


S.O. 4674(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, S.O. No. 3570 (E) Dated:22/08/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, 
Section 3, Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 956 (48 of 956) 
(hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in 
the Schedule annexed to the said notification for building (four-laning/Six laning, etc.), maintenance, management and 
operation of Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway NE-6 in the stretch of land from Km. I!.000 to Km. 28.050 in the district 
of LUCKNOW in the state of UTTAR PRADESH 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Dainik Bhaskar (Hindi)” and “The 
Times of India (English)” both dated 3! August, 2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (.) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


S.O. 4668(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Petroleum and 
Natural Gas, published in the Gazette of India No. 4050 on 9" September 2022, Part-II, Section 3, Sub Section (ii) vide 
S.O. 423] (E) dated 7" September 2022 and Gazette of India No. 2595, Part-II, Section -3, Sub-Section (ii) dated 20th 
June 2023 vide 8.0. No. 2709 (E) dated 20th June, 2023, issued under sub-section (l) of section 3 of the Petroleum and 
Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 962 (50 of 962), (hereinafter referred to as the said 
Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule 
appended to that notification for the Purpose of laying of Pipeline from Chudva to Panipat under New Mundra - Panipat 
Pipeline Project by Indian Oil Corporation Limited in Tehsil- Dhod, Lakshmangarh of District Sikar, Tehsil - 
Jhunjhunu, Mandawa, Nawalgarh, Surajgarh of District Jhunjhunu and Tehsil- Didwana, Choti Khatu of 
District Didwana-Kuchaman in the State of Rajasthan, for transportation of Crude oil. 


And whereas copies of the said Gazette notification were made available to the public. And whereas, under 
sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act the Competent Authority has submitted report to the Central Government. 


And whereas, the Central Government, after considering the said report and on being satisfied that the said 
land is required for laying the pipeline, has decided to acquire right of user therein. 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act, the 
Central Government hereby declares that the right of user in the said Land specified in the Schedule appended to this 
notification is hereby acquired for laying the pipeline.

NH227B के कि.मी. 47.800 से कि.मी. 73.300(PKG- गा) तक के भू-खण्ड के निर्माण (चौड़ीकरण/पेग्ड शोल्डर सहित 


2-लेन/4-लेन का बनाना आदि),अनुरक्षण, प्रबंधन और प्रचालन के लिए उस अधिसूचना से उपाबद्ध अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट 
भूमि का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी ;

उसका उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया;

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


9.0. 4676(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 2552(E) Dated:02/07/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for construcion (widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc..), 
maintenance, management and operation of NH227B in the stretch of land from Km 47.800 to Km.73.300(PKG- 
गा) in the district of AMBEDKAR NAGAR in the state of UTTAR PRADESH. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in "TheTimes of India''(English) and 
“Aaj” (Hindi) both dated 27th July 2024 under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


14 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

का.आ. 4677(अ).--- केन्द्रीय सरकार ने, राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग अधिनियम, 1956 (1956 का 48) (जिसे इसमें इसके 
पश्चात्‌ उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 3क की उपधारा (1) के अधीन जारी की गई भारत सरकार के सड़क 
परिवहन और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 1289 तारीख 12/03/2024, जो भारत के राजपत्र, 
असाधारण, भाग 1, खण्ड 3, उपखंड (ii) F प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा झारखंड राज्य के रामगढ जिले में NH320B के 
कि.मी. 53.6 से कि.मी. 71.323 (रामगढ़) तक के राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग के निर्माण (चौड़ा करने / चार लेन का बनाने, आदि), 
अनुरक्षण, TAIT और प्रचालन के लिए उस अधिसूचना से उपाबद्ध अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का अर्जन करने के अपने 
आशय की घोषणा की थी ; 


और उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3क की उपधारा (3) के अधीन तारीख "17.03.2024" 
को "द टाइम्स आफ़ इण्डिया" और "रांची एक्सप्रेस" दोनों में प्रकाशित किया गया था ; 


जबकि सक्षम प्राधिकारी को धारा 3-ग के तहत दायर आपत्ति प्राप्त हुई है, जिस पर विचार किया गया है और 
उसका उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया; 


6962 GI/2024 (1) 


2 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (1) के अनुसरण में, केन्द्रीय सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है; 


अतः अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, सक्षम प्राधिकारी की उक्त रिपोर्ट प्राप्त हो जाने पर और उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ 
की उपधारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह घोषणा करती है कि उक्त अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का 
पूर्वोक्त प्रयोजन के लिए अर्जन किया जाना चाहिए ; 


और अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (2) के अनुसरण में यह घोषणा करती है कि 
इस अधिसूचना के राजपत्र में प्रकाशन पर, उक्त अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि सभी विल्लंगमों से मुक्त होकर आत्यन्तिक रूप 
से केन्द्रीय सरकार में निहित हो जाएगी ।

section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and operation of 
Chilakaluripet - Vijayawada section of NH-16 from Km. 380.600 to Km. 432.650 in the district of Guntur in the state 
of Andhra Pradesh. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Prajasakti (Telugu)” and “The Hans 
India (English)” both dated 18.08.2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas no objection has been received from any person by the competent authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that 
on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall vest absolutely in 
the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi the 25th October, 2024 


S.O. 4681(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 4051 Dated:19/09/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and operation 
of NH-154 in the stretch of land from Km. 85.135 to Km. 100.840 in the villages namely Malan ambari, Ambari 
Jhikali, Pankhar, Ambari Upperli, Gujrehra, Barhai, Laleshar, Malan Khas (Land Acquisition Nagrota Bagwan) in the 
district of KANGRA in the state of Himachal Pradesh. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification 8.0. 4051(E) dated 19/09/2024 has been published in 
“Himachal Dustak” and “Times of India” both dated 0//10/2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


9.0. 4673(E).—Whereas by notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural 
Gas S.O.No. 877(E) dated 29.04.2024, issued under sub-section (l) of section 3 of the Petroleum and Minerals 
Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 962 (50 of 962), (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), 
published in the Extra Ordinary Gazette of India No. 785 dated 30.04.2024, the Government of India declared its 
intention to acquire the Right of User in the land specified in the Schedule appended to that notification for the purpose 
of laying pipeline for transportation of crude oil through Paradip — Numaligarh crude oil pipeline in the state of Assam 
by Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL). 


And whereas copies of the said Extraordinary Gazette notification were made available to the public. 


And whereas the objections received from the public to the laying of the pipeline have been considered and 
disposed by the Competent Authority. 


And whereas the Competent Authority has, under sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act submitted its 
report to the Government of India. 


And whereas the Government of India after considering the said report and on being satisfied that the said land 
is required for laying the pipeline, has decided to acquire right of user therein; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) of the section 6 of the said Act, the 
Government of India hereby declares that the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule appended to this 
notification is hereby acquired for laying the pipeline; 


And further, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 6 of the said Act, the Government 
of India hereby directs that the Right of User in the land for laying the pipeline shall, instead of vesting in Government 
of India, vest, on this date of the publication of the declaration, in the Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL), free from 
all encumbrances.

और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 2397 (अ) , तारीख 20 जून 2024, जो भारत के राजपत्र, असाधारण, 
भाग ॥, खण्ड 3, उपखंड (1) में प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा राजस्थान राज्य के राजसमंद जिले में राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग संख्या 8 
के 177.000 कि.मी. से 245.000 कि.मी. (गौमती चौराहा से उदयपुर सेक्शन) तक के भूखण्ड के निर्माण (चौड़ा करने / 
चार लेन का बनाने, आदि), अनुरक्षण, प्रबंधन और प्रचालन के लिए उस अधिसूचना से उपाबद्ध अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि 
का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी ; ; 


और उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3क की उपधारा (3) के अधीन 03 जुलाई 2024 को 
“दैनिक भास्कर” और “राजस्थान पत्रिका” दोनों ही में प्रकाशित किया गया था ; 


जबकि सक्षम प्राधिकारी को धारा 3-ग के तहत दायर आपत्ति प्राप्त हुई है, जिस पर विचार किया गया है और उसका 
उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया;

रिपोर्ट दे दी है; 


अतः अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, सक्षम प्राधिकारी की उक्त रिपोर्ट प्राप्त हो जाने पर और उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ 
की उपधारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह घोषणा करती है कि उक्त अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का पूर्वोक्त 
प्रयोजन के लिए अर्जन किया जाना चाहिए ; 

और अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (2) के अनुसरण में, यह घोषणा करती है कि 
इस अधिसूचना के राजपत्र में प्रकाशन पर उक्त अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि, सभी विल्लंगमों से मुक्त होकर आत्यन्तिक रूप से 
केन्द्रीय सरकार में निहित हो जाएगी ।

New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


S.O. 4685(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways, Number S.O. 2397 (E) dated 20.06.2024, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part वी, Section 
3, Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) 
(hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in 
the Schedule annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and 
operation of National Highway No. 8 on the stretch of land from Km 177.000 to Km 245.000 (Gomati Chauraha- 
Udaipur Section) in the district of Rajsamand in the state of Rajasthan. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Rajasthan Patrika” and “Dainik 
Bhaskar” both dated 03.07.2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and settled 
the same appropriately;

And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall vest 
absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


9.0. 4678(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, S.0.2390 Dated:20/06/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and operation 
of NH63 in the stretch of land from Km. 55 to Km. 69.25 (Armoor-Jagtial-Mancherial Section) in the district of 
JAGTIAL in the state of TELANGANA 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Mana Telangana” Telugu Daily 
and “The Hindu” English Daily both dated /Oth July, 2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And Whereas no objection has been received from any person by the Competent Authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (.) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 25th October, 2024 


S.O. 4683(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section 
(1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act),Vide 
S.O. No. 2321 (E) dated 14 JUNE 2024 the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in 
the Schedule annexed to the said notification for construction of (Widening/two lane with paved shoulder/ four laning 
etc.) maintenance, management and operation of NH731A (RAM VAN GAMAN PATH) on the stretch of land from 
Km 112.950 to Km 147.200 And Left limb (Chitrakoot by pass length 8.300 km) (Competent authority/Additional Sub 
Divisional Magistrate,Karvi) in the district of Chitrakoot in the state of UTTAR PRADESH ; 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “AAJ ” and “ THE TIMES OF 
INDIA" both dated 29" JUNE 2024 , under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas objections have been received and the same have been considered and disallowed by the competent 
authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall vest 
absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

पश्चात्‌ उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 3क की उपधारा (1) के अधीन जारी की गई भारत सरकार के सड़क 
परिवहन और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 3146(E) तारीख 06/08/2024, जो भारत के राजपत्र, 
असाधारण, भाग ॥, खण्ड 3, उपखंड (1) में प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा उड़ीसा राज्य के जाजपुर जिले में NH20 के कि.मी. 
0 से कि.मी. 49.2 (एटी / पीओ / पीएस / जिला- जाजपुर) तक के भूखण्ड पर टोल प्लाजा के निर्माण, अनुरक्षण, प्रबंधन 
और प्रचालन के लिए उस अधिसूचना से उपाबद्ध अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा की 
थी; 


और उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3क की उपधारा (3) के अधीन तारीख "२४/०८/२०२४" 
को "प्रमेय" और "प्रगतिबादी" दोनों में प्रकाशित किया गया था ; 


जबकि सक्षम प्राधिकारी को धारा 3-ग के तहत दायर आपत्ति प्राप्त हुई है, जिस पर विचार किया गया है और 
उसका उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (1) के अनुसरण में, केन्द्रीय सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है; 


अतः अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, सक्षम प्राधिकारी की उक्त रिपोर्ट प्राप्त हो जाने पर और उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ 
की उपधारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह घोषणा करती है कि उक्त अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का 
पूर्वोक्त प्रयोजन के लिए अर्जन किया जाना चाहिए ;

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi the 25th October, 2024 


9.0. 4666(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 3146(E) Dated:06/08/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for construction of Toll Plaza Maintenance, management and operation of NH20 in 
the stretch of land from Km. 0 to Km. 49.2 (AT/PO/PS/District- Jajpur) in the district of Jajpur in the state of 
ODISHA 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “PRAMEYA” and 
“PRAGATIBADI” both dated 24/08/2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 


vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

New Delhi the 25th October, 2024 


S.O. 4667(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, S.O. 603(E) Dated 2.02.2024, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, 
Sub- section (ii) issued under sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 956 (48 of I956) 
(hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in

the Schedule annexed to the said notification for building of four/six laning of Newly proposed Bangalore - Mydakuru 
(Kadapa) - Amarvathi/Vijayawada Greenfield Corridor in the stretch of land from Km. 0.000 to Km. 75.000 in the 
district of Sri Satya sai in the state of ANDHRA PRADESH. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “The Hans India” and “Prajasakthi” 
both dated 22.02.2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; And whereas objections have been 
received and the same have been considered and disallowed by the competent Authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (.) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

गया हो, जिसमें दंड भी शामिल है, वह विनियमन 61 के उप-विनयम (4) के अधीन, किसी भी अवधि की परिलब्धियों के 
बराबर की राशि का भुगतान प्राप्त करने के लिए पात्र होगा। 


यह भी प्रावधान किया जाता है कि जहां कोई अधिकारी या कर्मचारी सेवा छोड़ देता है या काम पर आना बंद कर

लिए पात्र होगा, यह अवधि अधिकतम 120 दिन तक की ही हो सकती है।.”

MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 28th October, 2024 


SUBJECT: PM-eBus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) scheme for Procurement and Operation of 
Electric Buses 


59.0. 47l(E).—. Introduction: Government of India has approved the PM-eBus Sewa-Payment Security 
Mechanism scheme (hereinafter called as ‘Scheme’) to establish a Payment Security Mechanism Fund (hereinafter 
called as ‘Scheme Fund’) for Procurement and Operation of electric buses (e-Bus) under the Gol/State Govt/UT 
sponsored schemes. This will mitigate the risk of payment delays and enhance the bankability for OEMs/operators who 
have entered into Concession Agreements (CAs)! with Public Transport Authorities (PTAs)? . 


2. Objectives: 


. Provide payment security in case of default by PTAs in making timely payment to the operators as per the 
CA executed between the PTAs and the OEM/operators 


i. Provide a mechanism for recouping of Scheme Funds from the parent State Governments/UTs in the event 
of non-repayment by PTAs. This will ensure sustainability of the Scheme Fund. 


ii. | Provide support in capacity building, training needs and adoption of innovative technologies by PTAs for 
e-bus operation. 


3. Salient Features of the Scheme: 
3. Coverage: 
The Scheme aims to cover 38,000 e-buses or more. 
3.2 Target Beneficiaries: 
The beneficiaries of the Scheme shall be the PTAs and the OEMs/operators who operate e-buses under the Scheme. 
3.3 Eligibility criteria: 
The eligibility criteria for PTAs, OEMs/operators to participate in the Scheme is explained below: 
3.3. Eligibility criteria for PTAs: 
PTAs meeting the following criteria will be eligible to participate in this Scheme: 
(a) the PTAs adopt the Gross Cost Contract (GCC) model for procurement of e-buses which is aligned with Scheme 
guidelines. However, PTAs procuring buses through any other similar model may also be considered subject 


to approval by the steering committee, and 
(b) their parent States/UTs register the Direct Debit Mandate (DDM) with RBI. Under DDM, the States/UTs 


l CAs refers to the agreements executed between PTAs and OEM/operators, by whatever name called 


(such as Agreements, Contract Agreement, etc), for procurement / deployment / operation / maintenance of the electric 
buses 


2 PTAs such as State Transport Undertakings (STUs), State Transport Corporations (STCs), Special Purpose Vehicles 
(SPVs), and any other Govt. agencies operating the bus service in India. 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


undertake to recoup the Scheme Fund as defined in the Scheme guidelines. The DDM submitted under the 
Scheme, will be valid for all Gol sponsored schemes for procurement and operation of e-buses, and 

(c) PTAs procure and operate e-buses with aggregation by Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL) under 
any Gol/State Govt/UT scheme where the CA adheres to the Scheme guidelines, or 

(d) In case PTAs are directly procuring e-buses (without CESL), adhering to PSM guidelines, then their request 
for participation under the Scheme can be considered by the steering committee (SC). 


3.3.2 Eligibility criteria for OEMs/operators: 


Those OEMs/operators who enter into CAs with PTAs satisfying eligibility criteria as mentioned at para 3.3.! shall be 
eligible for availing the Scheme Fund. 


3.4 Duration of the Scheme: 


The Scheme shall provide payment security coverage for up to 2 years for each bus deployed under the Scheme. 


4. Scheme Outlay: 


The total financial outlay under the Scheme shall be = 3,435.33 crore. 


5. Implementation Mechanism: 


5. Process to avail Scheme Fund by e-bus OEMs/operators: 


i. 


il. 


lil. 


Vi. 


PTAs shall open and maintain an Escrow Account as specified in the CA. 


The OEM/operators will submit a regular bill/invoice to PTAs in accordance with the timelines specified 
in the CA. 


The PTAs shall process the bill/invoice in accordance with the provisions of the CA. 


If insufficient funds in the Escrow Account result in delay/non-payment by PTAs within the prescribed 
time as per CA, then the event will be called as “Default by PTA”. 


Such defaults by PTAs will be reported to CESL and the OEM/operators may submit a request to CESL 
(PSM Request) to invoke the Payment Security Mechanism under the Scheme. 


CESL shall develop, operate and maintain a technology-based platform for the entire duration of the 
Scheme, that shall enable the OEMs/operators to submit their request for invoking the Scheme Fund. 


5.2 Process for fund disbursement from the Scheme to e-bus OEM/operators: 


i. 


il. 


iil. 


Process of fund disbursement along with the quantum and timelines will be detailed under Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs). 


CESL shall review, verify and approve the PSM request of OEM/operators. 


If CESL finds that the request of the OEM/operators is in accordance with CA, Scheme guidelines and the 
SOPs, then CESL shall disburse the approved amount from the Scheme Fund to the Escrow Account created 
under CA. 


5.3 Repayment mechanism to PSM by PTAs/ States/UTs in case of default by PTAs: 


The repayment mechanism by the PTAs/ States/UTs to Scheme Fund is as follows: 


i. 


Repayment from PTAs to Scheme: 


a. 


PTAs are required to repay to the Scheme Fund, the entire amount disbursed from the Scheme Fund to 
the OEM/operators along with Late Payment Surcharge (LPS), within 90 days from the date of its 
disbursement. 


During this period, PTAs will be levied an interest in the form of late payment surcharge (LPS), on the 
amount to be repaid. 


The LPS would be levied @% per annum in addition to the SBI’s 3 years MCLR prevailing on the date 
of disbursement, compounded annually. 


The number of days of delay for which LPS will be applicable will start from the date of disbursement 
from Scheme Fund to OEM/operators up to the date of payment received from the PTAs/State 
Govts/UTs.

ii. Recouping of Scheme Fund by State/UT through Direct Debit Mandate (DDM): 


a. In case the PTAs fails to repay the entire amount disbursed from the Scheme Fund along with Late 
Payment Surcharge (LPS) within 90 days from the disbursement date, MHI would request RBI to invoke 
the DDM. 


b. | RBI would transfer the money to the Scheme Fund by debiting the account of the State Government/UTs, 
subject to availability of clear and sufficient balance in the account at the time of executing the mandate. 
Clear balance in the account of State Government means the amount held in such account excluding 
minimum balance, operating limit under special drawing facility, authorised limit under ways and means 
advances and overdraft. 


छः This will also include the LPS as mentioned at para 5.3, (i), (०). 


d. The number of days of delay for which LPS will be applicable will start from the date of disbursement 
of Scheme Funds to OEMs/operators up to the date of transfer of money to the Scheme Fund by debiting 
the account of State Governments/UTs. 


6. Steering Committee (SC): 
To ensure effective operation and implementation of the Scheme, a steering committee has been constituted as under:

7. Implementing Agency — CESL: 
Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL) will be the implementing agency for the Scheme. 
8. Guidelines to the Scheme: 


For the effective operation and smooth implementation of the Scheme, the detailed guidelines shall be issued separately.

Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962, (50 of 1962) Government of India hereby declares its

of which the copies of the notification issued under sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the said Act, as published in the 
Gazette of India are made available to the general public, object in writing to the acquisition of the right of User 
therein for laying of the pipeline under the land to Competent Authority, GAIL (India) Limited.

RATING OF PROPERTIES FOR DIGITAL CONNECTIVITY 
REGULATIONS, 2024 (7 of 2024 ) 
SECTION-I 
PRELIMINARY 


l. Short title, extent and commencement.— (l) These regulations may be called the Rating of 
Properties for Digital Connectivity Regulations, 2024. 


(2) These regulations shall apply to - 


(i) property managers who intend to get their property, of minimum specified size, rated for 
digital connectivity, either voluntarily or under the provisions of applicable laws, rules or 
regulations; 


(ii) digital connectivity rating agencies, who may evaluate and award ratings for property 
under these regulations; and 


(iii) the service providers, who may enter into an arrangement with the property manager for 
development or access of digital connectivity or digital connectivity infrastructure. 


(3) They shall come into force from 25" October 2024. 
2. Definitions. — (/) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, -- 
(a) “Act” means the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 997 (24 of 997); 


(b) “Authority” means the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India established under sub- section (l) 
of section 3 of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 997;

(d) “digital connectivity infrastructure” or “DCI” means passive and active elements, which 
include any apparatus, appliance, instrument, equipment and system used or capable of extending 
seamless digital connectivity:

such as Radio Access Networks (RAN) and Wi-Fi systems, and Transmission Links Interface, Duct

(e) “digital connectivity rating agency” or “DCRA” means an eligible entity duly empaneled with the

(f) “entity” means a company registered under the Companies Act, 203 (8 of 203) or a registered 
LLP firm; 


(g) "person" means an individual, any company or association or body of individuals, whether 
incorporated or not, by whatsoever name called or referred to; 


(h) “property” means the properties provided under regulation 3 and includes buildings and their

(i) “property manager” means the person who is either the owner of the property to be rated for

(0) “public Wi-Fi network” means family of wireless network protocols commonly used for

(k) “Quality of Service” or “QoS” means main indicator of the performance of a telecommunication

Impartiality and independence: DCRA shall remain impartial and independent during digital 
connectivity assessment and entire rating process. DCRA should not have any financial interest or 
ownership or operational interests in the property under evaluation and assessment. DCRA shall 
establish policy and procedures for reviewing the work of its agents/employees to ensure 
independence of evaluation and assessment without external influences. 


Transparency and disclosure: DCRAs shall maintain documented process for evaluation and 
assessment of digital connectivity as specified by the Authority and disclose all relevant information 
about their evaluation and assessment methodologies. DCRA shall maintain verifiable historical 
information, in electronic form, about ratings awarded by it during the validity of ratings. 


Compliance with regulations: DCRAs shall strictly adhere to the regulations, guidelines, and 
standards set forth by the Authority for the digital connectivity rating system. 


Data privacy and security: DCRAs shall implement robust data privacy and security measures to 
protect sensitive information collected during digital connectivity assessments and comply with all 
relevant data privacy regulations. 


Qualified personnel: DCRAs shall employ qualified and certified professionals with the necessary 
expertise and experience to conduct digital connectivity assessment as per the provisions of the 
regulations. DCRA shall ensure regular training and upskilling of its concerned employees to 
account for technological upgradations. 


Fair and non-discriminatory practices: DCRAs shall ensure that the process for evaluation and 
assessment of the property and award of rating is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. The 
DCRAs shall also ensure that the fees charged by them are fair and without discrimination to any 
property managers regardless of the type of property or ownership. 


Clear fee structure: DCRAs shall establish a clear and transparent fee structure for different 
categories of properties as per regulations. Maximum chargeable fees (MCF) should be 
commensurate with the scope of work, and not excessive. MCF should be based on the complexity 
and size of the property. The broad fee structure and criteria shall be displayed on the rating platform 
to all relevant stakeholders. 


Conflict resolution mechanism: DCRAs shall establish a transparent mechanism for addressing 
conflicts and disputes with property managers. This mechanism should ensure a fair and unbiased 
resolution of issues. 


Compliance with building Bye-Laws: DCRAs shall ensure that their assessments align with the 
building bye-laws and other relevant regulations. 


Continuous improvement: DCRAs shall commit to ongoing improvements in their assessment 
methodologies by staying updated with technological advancements and adapting to industry best 
practices. 


Conflict of interest: DCRA shall not rate a property that has a stake in the DCRA or its associated 
business. DCRA shall not undertake evaluation, assessment and rating of any property which may 
result in potential conflict of interest with property owners or property manager, infrastructure 
providers, or service providers, which may directly or indirectly affect the transparency of the rating 
process. 


Review of ratings: DCRA shall institute a formal system of any review of ratings under provisions 
of regulations. The review shall not be taken up by the same personnel involved in initial ratings. 


Ethical marketing and advertising: DCRA shall not use any unethical means for marketing and 
shall not misrepresent its role or capabilities.

SCHEDULE-II 
Terms and conditions for fair use of rating and rating certificate 


Ratings are non-transferable: The ratings are awarded to specific property and are non- 
transferable. Therefore, the ratings shall only be used for the specific property to which it has been 
awarded. 


Use in marketing and promotion: The property managers can use the awarded ratings in their 
marketing and promotional materials, including brochures, websites, and advertisements. However, 
the ratings shall be used accurately and in a non-misleading manner. 


Non-alteration: The property managers shall not alter or represent the rating certificates in any way 
that could be misleading in any manner whatsoever. 


Periodic updates: The property managers shall always use the valid ratings and update their rating 
certificates periodically as and when there is any change. 


Disclosure of ratings: The property managers shall either suo moto disclose the ratings to their 
users/owners/tenants or provide the details as and when demanded. 


Compliance with regulatory requirements: The property managers should adhere to any 
regulatory requirements related to the use of ratings, ensuring that they do not violate any laws or 
regulations. 


Usage within validity period: The property manager is authorized to use the ratings or rating 
certificates only during the validity period of the certificate. Use of ratings or rating certificates after 
the validity period shall be considered as misuse of the certificate and be construed as contravention 
of the regulations.

Explanatory Memorandum 
Background 


Digital connectivity is crucial to our modern life and work. The exponential growth in digitalization 
over the past decade has revolutionized the world, affecting everything from the economy, innovation, 
science, and education to health, sustainability, governance, and lifestyle. Digital technologies are 
fundamentally transforming business models, institutions, and society. 


The demand for digital connectivity has indeed increased in recent years, and this trend was 
particularly evident during the COVID-l9 pandemic. The pandemic highlighted the essential role of 
digital connectivity, as it became a lifeline for many aspects of daily life. With lockdowns and social 
distancing measures in place, people relied heavily on digital technologies for work, education, 
healthcare, and social interaction. This sudden shift underscored the importance of robust and 
accessible digital infrastructure for all users, regardless of their location. The increased demand across 
various segments, from urban to rural areas, demonstrated the necessity for widespread and reliable 
internet access to support a digitally connected society. 


The proportion of data consumed inside buildings and outside is shifting significantly towards 
consumption of data inside the buildings. Accordingly, we need to have robust and good quality 
telecom network coverage/ connectivity in indoor areas. With Work from Home (WFH) or Work from 
Anywhere (WFA) at any time becoming the new norm, the need for ubiquitous and good quality of 
digital connectivity inside buildings has gained considerable momentum in recent times. 


Digital connectivity plays a pivotal role in modern society by: 


(i) Facilitating Communication: Enables instant communication across the globe, connecting people 
and businesses effortlessly. 


(ii) Supporting Remote Work and Education: Allows for remote working and online learning, 
providing flexibility and access to resources irrespective of location. 


(iii) Driving Economic Growth: Fuels innovation and entrepreneurship, opening new markets and 
business models. 


(iv) Enhancing Healthcare: Enables telemedicine and digital health services, improving access to 
medical care and information. 


(v) Promoting Social Inclusion: Bridges the digital divide, providing equal opportunities for all, 
including marginalized communities. 


(vi) Advancing Governance: Improves public services and governance through digital platforms, 
enhancing transparency and efficiency. 


(vii) Enabling Smart Technologies: Supports the development and implementation of smart 
technologies in various sectors like transportation, agriculture, and energy. 


(Vili) Fostering Global Collaboration: Encourages international collaboration in science, 
education, and other fields, driving collective progress. 


(ix) Boosting Sustainability: Facilitates sustainable practices and green technologies, contributing to 
environmental conservation. Overall, digital connectivity is a cornerstone of contemporary life, 
shaping the way we interact, work, learn, and develop as a society. 


In India, there are 927.56 million wireless internet subscribers (as of June 2024) against 42.04 million 
internet subscribers having wired connectivity in their homes or offices. Thus, at present, the majority 
of the population is dependent on wireless networks to access the internet. Despite significant roll-out 
of the 4G (LTE) network and recent expansion of 5G network, availability of more spectrum bands, 
the coverage and quality of digital connectivity inside buildings remains a major issue which requires 
a completely new regulatory approach. 


To provide legal and regulatory trigger for addressing the issue of accessibility and quality of digital 
connectivity inside buildings, the Authority has submitted recommendations to the Government on 
“Rating of Buildings or Areas for Digital Connectivity” on 20th February 2023. The recommendations 
are aimed to create an ecosystem for co-creations of Digital Connectivity Infrastructure (DCD) as a part

Good digital connectivity which meets the expectations of end users is not a one-time exercise. It

for the increasing demand and adopt evolving telecom technologies. Exponential rise in demand for

creation of DCI, though handled, and resolved during laying of the infrastructure for the first time, will 
keep on reappearing every time expansion or upgradation of related activity is taken up. Such issues 
are to be dealt with during the entire lifecycle of a properties, as every issue cannot be fully envisaged 
in the initial phase of creation of digital connectivity.

Analysis and Conclusion: 


The Authority has noted that most of the stakeholders have agreed with the proposed criteria to be 
used for assessment digital connectivity and award of ratings for properties. The Authority is of the

towards the actual status of digital connectivity on the ground. Therefore, considering the inputs 
from the stakeholders, the weightage for compliance with MBBL has been reduced from 20 to 0 as 
it is an essential requirement. Further, the weightage for two parameters i.e. ‘Provision of Wired 
Connectivity infrastructure’ and ‘Availability of Service Providers’ has been increased from 0 to I5 
for each of them to have reflection of actual digital connectivity status in the ratings.

conduct for DCRA has been provided in the regulations in line with the inputs of the stakeholders. 


As the user experience is directly linked to the service performance, the criteria ‘User experience’ has 
been renamed as ‘Service Performance & User Experience’ to bring more objectivity in assessment. 
The weightage against this criterion has been increased from 0 to 20. The sub-criteria under this

public areas and upload/download speeds of wireline broadband.

F. No. BOA/3-B/PAP/2024.—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-cluases (h), (i), (j) and 
(zb) of section 55 of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020, (4 of 2020) read 
with regulation 9 of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (National Examination for 
Indian System of Medicine) Regulations 2023, the Commission hereby makes the following regulations, 
namely:- 


CHAPTER-I 
PRELIMANARY 


I. Short title and commencement.- () These regulations may be called the National Commission for Indian 
System of Medicine (Pre-Ayurveda-Programme for Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery) 
Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions.- (l) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, - 


(a) “Act” means the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020 (4 of 2020); 


24 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(b) “Seven and half years Ayurveda- Programme” means a residential graduation programme of two 
years of Pre-Ayurveda, four and half years of Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery and one 
year of compulsory rotatory internship and having provision for admission to under graduate course 
after tenth class through National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Pre-Ayurveda. 


(c) “Ayurveda Gurukulam” means a standalone residential Ayurveda institution or college along with the 
teaching hospital for total seven and half years Degree Program of Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine 
and Surgery along with two years Pre Ayurveda-Program; 


(d) “Annexure” means an annexure annexed to these regulations; 

(e) “Appendix” means an appendix appended to these regulations; 

(f) “Institution” means the Ayurveda Gurukulam; and 

(g) “NEET-PAP” means National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for Pre Ayurveda Programme. 


(2) The words and expressions used herein and not defined but defined in the Act shall have the same 
meanings as respectively assigned to them in the Act. 


3. General considerations. - (l) Seven and half years Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery 
program, to be conducted in the Ayurveda Gurukulam. 


(2) The institution shall be called Ayurveda Gurukulam with a prefix or suffix as the management desires. 
(3) All Ayurveda Gurukulams shall be affiliated to the Central Sanskrit University, Janakpuri, New Delhi. 


(4) The number of such Ayurveda Gurukulams shall be in proportion to the population of the States or 
Union territory. Administration for up to five-crore population, there shall be an another Ayurveda 
Gurukulam in the States or Union territory Administration. 


(5) The existing Ayurveda institutions and Ayurveda Gurukulam shall not be allowed to convert vice- 
versa. 


(6) Programmes offered in the Ayurveda Gurukulam shall be seven and half years Ayurveda 
undergraduate programme (Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery) along with two years Pre 
Ayurveda Program and only those courses that have been allowed by the Commission for Ayurveda 
Gurukulam shall be allowed in the Ayurveda Gurukulam premises. 


(7) (a) The Ayurveda Gurukulum shall install online systems such as Learning Management Systems; 
Hospital Information Management System (compatible with Ayushman Bharat Health Account, Health 
Professional Registry and Unique Health Identification number); Aadhaar Enabled Biometric 
Attendance System or iris recognition or face recognition attendance system and the like as directed by 
the Commission for marking attendance of Teaching staff, non-teaching staff, hospital staff and 
Undergraduate students; 


(b) Closed Circuit Television and any other systems as directed by the Commission from time to time, 
shall be installed and shall be aligned or interface to the Central server as designated by the 
Commission and shall provide real time data or relevant data to the Commission and its autonomous 
Boards as required; 


(c) the biometric attendance data shall be made available to the concerned regulatory body or the 
Commission or the Autonomous Boards of the Commission on real time basis throughout the year 
through any agency as assigned by the Commission 


(8) The authentication of the patients shall be made through the Ayushman Bharat Health Account 
number. 


(9) All the constructions in the Ayurveda Gurukulam shall depict traditional Gurukulam and shall follow 
green campus concepts.

UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMME 


0. Purpose of Pre-Ayurveda program is, - 


() to prepare the student to learn and understand Ayurveda, rooted in the relevant Bharateeya Shastras 
and Sanskrit language; 


(2) to prepare the student to study Ayurveda authentically from its classical sources and eventually to 
become a holistic practitioner; 


(3) to orient the student to imbibe the values of Indian culture and tradition through the Ayurveda 
Gurukulam model of education and; 


(4) to facilitate informal interaction between the Guru and Shishya as an important component of the 
teaching-learning process. 


i. Admission capacity. - The admission capacity for each Ayurveda Gurukulam shall be fifty seats for 
every academic session. 


2. Eligibility criteria for admission. - (॥) The eligibility for admission into seven and half years 
Programme for Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine Surgery shall be as under: 


(a) the candidate shall have passed 0" standard in 0+2 pattern; or in 5+3+3+4 pattern from any 
recognized Board including Sanskrit board of state or any equivalent recognized board; 


(b) no candidate shall be admitted to this Program unless he has attained the age of fifteen years on or 
before the 3‘' December of the year of his admission in the first year of the program. 


(2) There shall be a uniform entrance examination in Sanskrit or any other language as specified by the 
Commission from time to time for all Ayurveda Gurukulam for seven and half years Ayurveda 
undergraduate Program namely, the National Eligibility-cum-entrance Test Pre-Ayurveda Programme 
in each academic year and shall be conducted by an authority designated by the Commission, in order 
to consider eligible for admission to Pre-Ayurveda Programme, it shall be necessary for a general 
candidate to obtain minimum marks at fifty percent and at forty percent for the candidates belonging to 
the Scheduled Caste, the Scheduled Tribes, the other Backward classes and candidate with disabilities 
under the Rights of Person with disabilities Act, 20l6 (49 of 206) in the National Eligibility cum 
entrance Test Pre-Ayurveda for Pre-Ayurveda Programme held for the said academic year: 


Provided that where sufficient number of candidates in the respective category (Scheduled 
Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes) fail to secure minimum marks in the 
National Eligibility-cum-entrance Test- Pre-Ayurveda Programme held for any academic year for 
admission to Pre-Ayurveda Program, the Commission, may lower the minimum marks required 
for admission to Pre-Ayurveda Program for candidates belonging to respective category and 
marks so lowered shall be applicable for that academic year only. 


(3) An all India common merit list of the eligible candidates shall be prepared on the basis of the marks 
obtained in the National Eligibility-cum-entrance Test Pre-Ayurveda Programme and the candidates, 
within the respective category shall be considered for admission to Pre-Ayurveda Program from the 
said merit list only.

(4) The reservation for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes Category

(5) Online counselling for admission in to Pre-Ayurveda Programme shall be as specified in the National 
Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum standards of Undergraduate Ayurveda 
Education) Regulations, 2022, - 


(i) all seats irrespective of category Central quota, State Quota or management or any other quota as 
applicable except foreign nationals shall be admitted through online counselling only and direct

(ii) the institutions shall have to submit the list of students admitted in the format and time specified by 
the Commission from time to time for verification; 


(iii) Central Sanskrit University shall approve the admission of those candidates (except foreign 
nationals) who have been allotted through Online Counselling; 


(iv) no authority or institution shall admit any candidate to the seven and half years undergraduate 
Ayurveda Programme in contravention of the criteria or procedure laid down in these regulations 
in respect of admission and any admission made in contravention of the said criteria or procedure 
shall be cancelled by the Commission forthwith; 


(v) the authority or institution which grants admission to any student in contravention of the criteria or 
procedure laid down in these regulations shall be liable for disciplinary action under the relevant 
provisions of the Act; 


(vi)any other equivalent qualification for foreign national candidates may be allowed and _ the 
provisions under sub-regulation (2) of this regulation shall not be applicable to such candidates. 


3. Duration of the Program: - The Program shall be of seven and half years duration including two 
years of pre Ayurveda program. 
4. Pre-Ayurveda Program Certificate.- 


(l) The candidate shall be awarded Pre-Ayurveda Certificate on completion of duration of Pre- 
Ayurveda Programme and after passing of all the subjects laid down in Table-3 for Pre-Ayurveda 
Programme. 


(2) Pre-Ayurveda Certificate shall be equivalent to 0+2 Certificate and Pre-Ayurveda qualified 
candidates shall be eligible for those programs where the eligibility is 0+2 or its equivalent. 


5. Medium of instruction. - The medium of instruction for the Program shall be Sanskrit or Hindi or 
English or any recognized Indian regional languages in the 87 schedule to the constitution of India: 


Provided that, if any Ayurveda Gurukulam is admitting students from different states or 
international students, the medium of instruction shall be in Sanskrit or English. 


6. Mentor. -() There shall be a mentor for each group of 25 students and the same mentor shall 
continue for all the years of study in Ayurveda Gurukulam, if the mentor and student are not 
compatible with each other, then a fair chance shall be given to the student to change the mentor. 


(2) The mentor shall be a teacher of any subject, preferably with knowledge in Sanskrit with integrity 
and dedication to teaching. 


(3) He or she shall be responsible for the overall development of students. 
(4) He or she shall stay in the residential campus of the Ayurveda Gurukulam. 
(5) The mentor shall not be a warden of the student's hostel. 


(6) He or she shall be aware of adolescent psychology, Prakriti (sharirika and manasika) and human 
behavior. 


7. Pattern of study. - (!) This Program shall consist of main subjects and electives and the ratio of 
lecture to non-lecture hours shall be around :2 and the Ayurveda Gurukulam may offer different 
skill options for the students. 


(2) The formal education shall include course curriculum as per competency-based syllabus developed 
in accordance with the National Curriculum Framework based on the National Education Policy 
2020.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
[Western Railway (Construction Organization)] 
NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 28th October, 2024 
S.O. 4698(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section(i) of section 20A of the Railways Act, 

1989(24 of 1989) (here in after referred in as the said Act), the Central Government after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, this land of Village- Athar Tehsil-Dhar District- Dhar, the brief description of which has given in the 
schedule annexed here to, is required for execution of Special Railway Project for Indore- Dahod new BG railway line 
in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh state. Declares its intention to acquire such land in the State of Madhya Pradesh, 
hereby declares its intention to acquire such land: 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for a foresaid purpose under 
sub-section (1) of section 20D of the said Act: 

Every such objection shall be made to the competent authority, namely, Sub-Divisional Officer &Land 
Acquisition Officer, Tehsil Dhar District-Dhar (M.P.), in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the competent 
authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after 
hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any as the competent authority thinks necessary, 
by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 

Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (II) of section 20(D) of the said act shall be final. 


The Land Plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person aforesaid Office of the Competent Authority.

enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 29th October, 2024 


S.O. 4728(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways, 5.0. No. 2724 (E) dated 12" July 2024, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, 
Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for construction of 4-lanewith paved shoulder configuration of bypass to Ras town on 
National Highway-158 from Km 0.00 to Km 2.170 (Ras - Paliyawas Road ) in District Pali in the State of Rajasthan. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Dainik Navjyoti 
(Hindi)” and “Rajasthan Patrika (English)” both dated 02.08.2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said 
Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and settled 
the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall vest 
absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 29th October, 2024 


S.O. 473(E).—Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 2306(E) Dated:4/06/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for building (widening / four-laning, etc.) management and operation of NH52 (Old 
NH-2]8) on the stretch of land from Km. 33.00 to Km. 40.00 (Bijapur - Hubballi Section) in the district of 
GADAG in the state of KARNATAKA 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Vijayakarnataka,Prajavani” and 
“Deccan Hearald,Times of India” both dated 26-06-2024; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (.) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 29th October, 2024 


S.O. 474(E)—In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National 
Highways Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after 
being satisfied that for the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule 
below, is required for building (widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, 
management and operation of NH 752G in the stretch of land from Km 2.427 to Km 64.000 Pimpalner 
to Satana Road (Section-2) in the district of NASHIK in the state of MAHARASHTRA, hereby declares 
its intention to acquire such land. 

Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub- 
section(|) of section 3C of the said Act. 

Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Deputy Collector, Land 
Acquisition, National Highway Project, Nashik in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the 
Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a legal 
practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the 
Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 

Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be 
final.The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and 
can be inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 29th October, 2024 


59.0. 4737(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of NH61 in the 
stretch of land from Km. 9.8 to Km. 64 (Mohan Pride 2nd floor Cultural Center Near Potdar School, Khadakpada, 
Kalyan West) in the district of THANE in the state of MAHARASHTRA, hereby declares its intention to acquire such 
land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Sub Divisional Office Kalyan in 
writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of 
being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making 
such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be 
final. 

The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.
